- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.4) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.2) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for 5–10 days.
- Model consistently underestimates in low-sentiment, low-price regimes (e.g., <65); apply upward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 days.
- If 3–5 consecutive forecast days show downward trend, model often fails to reverse; add upward bias of 1–3% for next 3–5 days if sentiment turns positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 10–15 days’ values if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model overreacts; dampen forecast by 1–2% for 3–5 days after sentiment shifts.
